policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere כַּעֲלוֹת (k- + infinitive construct) and ketiv בעלות (b- + infinitive construct) are both temporal infinitival clauses meaning 'when/as they came up'; the prepositions are not distinguished in English. ASV renders 'when the priests ... were come up out of the midst of the Jordan', which fits either preposition, and JOS.4.18 carries no mapped textual note. Both readings retained; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
